newsitem.title: RUSSIA: First Yeltsin-Lebed meeting in month planned.
newsitem.headline: First Yeltsin-Lebed meeting in month planned.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin was scheduled to meet Alexander Lebed on Thursday for their first talks since the security supremo forged a peace deal with Chechen rebels over a month ago
The presidential press service said on Wednesday the meeting would take place in the hospital where Yeltsin is preparing for heart surgery.

The outspoken general, drafted by Yeltsin into his team in June after a strong showing in the first round of Russia's presidential election, has been seeking a meeting with his boss since the controversial peace deal was signed on August 31.

Lebed, who does not hide his presidential ambitions, has said Yeltsin should cede power while he is ill. He is increasingly critical of the way Russia is run and has hinted his own powers should be widened.

Lebed's deal with the rebels includes withdrawal of Russian troops and postponement of a decision on Chechnya's political status for five years. Opponents see it as capitulation to the separatists who seized the regional capital Grozny in August.
The fact that Yeltsin is now to meet Lebed may indicate that the Russian leader has regained some strength before the operation and is ready to demonstrate his grip on power.
